original_question: For a geometrically connected smooth projective surface X over a finite field, does the 2-primary torsion subgroup Br(X)(2) admit a non-degenerate alternating pairing with values in Q/Z?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in §1.1, proved as Theorem 1.2, namely that the canonical Artin-Tate pairing is alternating; Theorem 1.3 is the higher-dimensional generalization whose specialization to d=1 recovers the surface case.
correct_elements: Your draft gets the main mathematical theme right: it is about smooth projective surfaces over a finite field, the 2-primary Brauer group, and a Q/Z-valued alternating non-degenerate pairing.
missing_details: The paper asks about the specific canonical Artin-Tate pairing, not merely whether some non-degenerate alternating pairing exists.
The relevant group is not Br(X)(2) itself but Br(X)_nd[2^∞], where Br(X)_nd := Br(X)/Div Br(X) is the quotient by the maximal divisible subgroup.
The ambient field is written explicitly as a finite field F_q, and X is assumed smooth, projective, and geometrically connected over F_q.
For the 2-primary question one must assume char(F_q) = p ≠ 2, because the Artin-Tate pairing in the paper is defined for primes ℓ ≠ p, and the only nontrivial alternation issue is at ℓ = 2.
Non-degeneracy is not the open part of the statement: §2.1 recalls that the Artin-Tate pairing is already non-degenerate; the problem is whether this known skew-symmetric pairing is alternating.
The paper's notation is Br(X)_nd[ℓ^∞] (in particular Br(X)_nd[2^∞]), not Br(X)(2).
refined_question: For every smooth, projective, geometrically connected surface X over a finite field F_q with char(F_q) = p ≠ 2, if Br(X)_nd := Br(X)/Div Br(X), is the canonical Artin-Tate pairing ⟨·,·⟩_AT : Br(X)_nd[2^∞] × Br(X)_nd[2^∞] → Q/Z alternating?
justification: The draft is closest to Tate's Conjecture 1.1 in Feng's paper, not to Zarhin's earlier partial result. In §1.1, equation (1.1.1) introduces the Artin-Tate pairing for a smooth, projective, geometrically connected surface X/F_q on Br(X)_nd[ℓ^∞], and Conjecture 1.1 asks whether that pairing is alternating. Section 2.1, Definition 2.1 recalls that the pairing is already non-degenerate, so the paper's real question is alternation of the canonical pairing, not existence of an abstract pairing. Theorem 1.2 proves Conjecture 1.1, while Theorem 1.3 states the higher-dimensional version and specializes to surfaces when d = 1. Also, the supplied arXiv ID 1006.3304 resolves to an unrelated paper, so the mathematical draft and the internal label cues point instead to Feng's paper as the intended source.
